title: The Atlas of the Lower Danube
premise: In the river town of Vidin, 1875, Ivo Delacroix has survived by being nobody's business: the daughter of a dead typeface cutter, tolerated in her father's old print shop because she is useful and quiet. When the winter closes the bridge and the Ottoman garrison seals the town, a dying courier leaves her a satchel of testimonies about a massacre the authorities mean to erase, and Ivo must choose between the silences that kept her alive and the record that might keep others alive after her. Printing the truth means exposing the network of neighbors who sheltered her — the baker, the ferryman's widow, the garrison clerk who loved her father — to reprisal from a governor determined to control the story. As spring and the revolution arrive together, Ivo smuggles the printed atlas of testimonies across the thawing river, sacrificing the shop and nearly her life, and ends the book not as a ghost in someone else's story but as its keeper, among people who finally know her name.
about_author: Sebastian Iversen is the pen name of a former typesetter who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century letterpress equipment in workshops along the Danube. This is their third novel, and the first written entirely by hand before a single line touched a keyboard.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Letters
chapters.summary: Ivo, in her POV, sets type for a garrison proclamation and reflects on five years of learned invisibility since her father's death. Establishes the print shop, the town, and her rule of useful silence. Emotional beat: the ache of being competent but unseen.

chapters.title: What the River Carries
chapters.summary: From the ferryman's widow Mara's POV, the last crossing before the bridge closes; a wounded courier slips aboard among grain sacks. Ivo watches from the shop window, sensing the town's rhythm change. Emotional beat: unease beneath ordinary ritual.

chapters.title: The Satchel in the Loft
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV: the courier dies in the print shop's paper loft, pressing a satchel of testimonies into her hands with a name she doesn't recognize. She hides it where her father hid forbidden type. Emotional beat: terror and the first crack in her silence.

chapters.title: Governor's Ink
chapters.summary: The garrison clerk Emil, POV, is ordered to prepare an official account of 'bandit suppression' in the river villages — a sanitized version of the massacre. He recognizes the shop's typeface habits and grows suspicious of Ivo. Emotional beat: complicity curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: Bread and Questions
chapters.summary: Mara's POV: she brings Ivo bread and, over the loaves, admits she helped the courier. Two keepers of secrets recognize each other. Ivo shows her one testimony and immediately regrets it. Emotional beat: the risk and relief of being known.

chapters.title: The Atlas Her Father Drew
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV: sorting the satchel, she finds her father's hand-drawn maps of the river villages annotated with names — he had been collecting testimonies before his death. The massacre connects to what killed him. Emotional beat: grief recontextualized as inheritance.

chapters.title: A Census of the Living
chapters.summary: Emil's POV: the governor orders households registered and papers inspected before spring; the baker Stefan's forged ledgers begin to fray. Emil falsifies one line — the shop's — and hates himself for how easily he did it. Emotional beat: small treasons.

chapters.title: Learning to Read a Town
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV: she begins mapping who can be trusted, testing neighbors with small confidences, discovering the network her father built — the baker, the priest's widow, a boy who watches the bridge. Emotional beat: loneliness giving way to cautious belonging.

chapters.title: The Sermon That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mara's POV: a garrison chaplain delivers a sermon praising order in the villages; the congregation's silence becomes its own testimony. Mara realizes the town is choosing, together, what not to say. Emotional beat: collective grief as solidarity.

chapters.title: Type, Melted
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV: soldiers quarter in the shop; she melts down and hides her father's most distinctive type, keeping only enough to print. A young soldier catches her and says nothing. Emotional beat: the cost of the plan made physical.

chapters.title: What Emil Kept
chapters.summary: Emil's POV: he finds the courier's name in the governor's execution list and understands Ivo has the satchel. Instead of reporting her, he leaves a corrected page of the official account in her type case — a message in her own craft. Emotional beat: an enemy turning.

chapters.title: The Longest Night of Setting
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with Mara and the boy Jovan helping: the first night of printing the atlas of testimonies, page by page, by candlelight, while soldiers sleep upstairs. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose; found family forged at the press.

chapters.title: Snow on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Mara's POV: the river freezes solid enough to cross; a patrol nearly discovers the hidden pages in the ice cellar. Stefan the baker takes the blame for a broken seal and is arrested. Emotional beat: guilt, and the price of the network.

chapters.title: The Governor's Historian
chapters.summary: Emil's POV: an official historian arrives from the capital to finalize the victors' account, and Emil must hand over the town's records. He steals the massacre's true casualty list in the process. Emotional beat: the race between memory and erasure made explicit.

chapters.title: Stefan's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV: visiting Stefan's imprisoned household, she is tempted to flee with the finished atlas and let the town fend for itself. Jovan, who has been watching the bridge, shows her the thaw cracks in the ice — days, not weeks. Emotional beat: the temptation of survival against duty.

chapters.title: Confessions at the Press
chapters.summary: Emil comes to the shop at night and confesses what he knows and what he's stolen, offering the casualty list for the final signature. Ivo must decide whether a collaborator can belong. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a deliberate act, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Last Signature
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV: the final pages are set — her father's maps, the testimonies, the casualty list, and her own name as printer, the name she has hidden for five years. Emotional beat: claiming authorship of her own life.

chapters.title: Ice Going Out
chapters.summary: Mara's POV: the river breaks; the garrison moves to burn the shop as 'seditious premises.' The network scatters the printed atlas among grain barges, laundry, coffins. Stefan is freed in the chaos. Emotional beat: panic and fierce collective competence.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV: she stays to fire the press one last run as soldiers arrive; the shop burns, and Emil covers her escape at the cost of his own arrest. She crosses the thawing river with the atlas strapped to her body. Emotional beat: everything lost except what matters.

chapters.title: The Other Bank
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV: on the free bank, she delivers the atlas to the revolution's printers, who want to fold her testimony into their own narrative. She refuses to be anonymous again and insists the villagers' names stand as written. Emotional beat: the fight over memory continues, and she is now a combatant.

chapters.title: Historians, Victorious and Otherwise
chapters.summary: Emil's POV, from a cell: the official history is published without the massacre; but copies of Ivo's atlas move hand to hand, and he reads a smuggled page by candlelight, knowing his treason held. Emotional beat: hope without vindication.

chapters.title: A Shop of Her Own
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, a year later: in a rebuilt river town, with Mara, Jovan, and a freed Stefan, she opens a small press under her own name, printing the atlas's second edition and a school primer. Emotional beat: belonging earned, memory kept, silence finally chosen rather than imposed.
